messages:
alex: Quick report — installed redwoodctl via the macOS pkg and local login keeps redirecting to http://localhost:8085 but the callback never hits the CLI. Browser shows ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

mara: Which installer — Homebrew or the pkg from releases?

alex: pkg from releases (redwoodctl-0.9.1-macos.pkg). I also have an older /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl from a manual unzip. Path ordering might be weird.

jon: Could be two binaries shadowing each other. `which redwoodctl`?

alex: `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` — but the pkg put a binary in /opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl and a symlink in /usr/local/bin pointing to it. The old copy is still there.

sophie: If the old exe is older it might be trying to spin up the callback server on a different port (we changed the default listener from 8085 -> 8087 recently).

alex: Good call. I nuked the old binary and re-run `redwoodctl login --local-serve`. Now browser opens but macOS blocks it with “redwoodctl wants to accept incoming network connections” and it fails silently. The CLI shows:

```
Waiting for auth callback...
Error: listen EACCES: permission denied 0.0.0.0:8087
```

mara: macOS firewall prompt usually appears the first time an app tries to listen. If the binary moved it can trigger the dialog. But the pkg binary should be signed. Did notarization/signing change?

alex: Signed, but I had to manually allow in System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Firewall → Allow incoming connections. After that login flow completed.

sam: Two follow-ups: 1) we should surface a clearer error when bind fails (EACCES) telling users to check macOS firewall / binary move; 2) the installer should detect and remove/rename old copies under PATH or warn during postinstall.

mara: Agreed. Also suggest a headless fallback message for CI/airgapped devs. Right now the CLI prints nothing helpful and folks assume the auth server is broken.

jon: We have env flags but not documented well. For headless auth the env var is REDWOODCTL_DEVICE_CODE=1 which triggers device-code flow and prints the code + URL. There's also REDWOODCTL_NO_BROWSER=1.

sophie: Can we make the CLI auto-detect firewall EACCES and print a one-liner: “macOS firewall may be blocking redwoodctl. Go to System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Firewall to allow incoming connections”?

sam: Yes — small PR. Also add a post-install check in the pkg script to scan for other `redwoodctl` executables in PATH and warn, e.g.:

```sh
for p in $(which -a redwoodctl); do
  if [ "$(realpath $p)" != "/opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl" ]; then
    echo "Found another redwoodctl at $p — this can cause auth or completion issues"
  fi
done
```

alex: Another gotcha: my sample-app dev.env had REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai/ but local-serve expects REDWOODCTL_API_URL — trivial but tripped me up on onboarding sample. Can we alias?

mara: We should document both envs and have the local server accept REDWOOD_API_URL as a fallback. Low-risk change.

jon: I'll pick up the CLI EACCES message and the sample-app env alias. sam, can you open an installer issue for the postinstall warning and a docs PR for the headless flags?

sam: Yep — filing now. Issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1428 : add PATH-scan postinstall warning + docs note about firewall.

devops-bot: Deploy bot: pre-release redwoodctl-0.9.2-alpha built for macOS (signed). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/2345

sophie: Nice. Let's also add a tiny note to the Quickstart: "If the auth browser fails, try REDWOODCTL_DEVICE_CODE=1 redwoodctl login or check macOS Firewall permissions."

alex: Thanks all — flow worked after removing old binary + allowing firewall. Will test the alpha pkg and report any differences. :thumbsup:
